## 1. Purpose, scope and roles

Convert agreed priorities into measurable outcomes, resourced actions and reliable performance review. Objectives are not lists of documents to write.

Process identity: **P04**. Accountable process owner: **Objective owner**.
The roles in the table perform the work. Actual appointments and deputies must be
recorded before adoption; fictional names in the example are not appointments.
This is an administrative IMS workflow, not permission to operate, isolate, repair
or restart chemical equipment.

## 2. Trigger and prerequisites

**Trigger:** Initial planning, management review, changed context/risk or evidence that an existing target is inappropriate.

**Required inputs/resources:** Agreed scope, policy commitments, risks and obligations, available baseline data and delegated budget/decision authority. Unknown baseline is an investigation task, not zero performance.

## 3. Process map and controlled steps

Choose outcome → establish baseline → define measure/target → resource plan → approve → collect data → evaluate and adjust without erasing history

Use the [worksheet](ORR-FRM-OBJ-001_SET-OBJECTIVES-AND-DELIVERY-PLANS-WORKSHEET.md). Each row below is a discrete proposed control:
who and when are explicit; the action/method and acceptance test are in the step;
where is the scoped process and its authorized private record store; why is the
purpose above, refined to the linked objective/risk in each execution record.
Copy each adopted control into the risk/control register with its own stable ID.

| Step | Performer | Trigger/frequency | Action and method/criteria | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Objective owner | Before proposing a target | Explain the desired outcome and linked risk/commitment. Define population, units, numerator/denominator where relevant, data owner and source; establish a dated baseline or a baseline collection action. | Objective record and baseline evidence. |
| 2 | Objective owner with affected process owners | Before management approval | Propose target and deadline, milestones, resources, delivery owners and safeguards against misleading results. Distinguish activity measures from outcome measures. | Delivery plan, dependencies and measurement definition. |
| 3 | Management sponsor | At planning/review decision | Check feasibility, resources and unintended effects. Approve the exact target/plan or return it with reasons. An unresourced aspiration stays proposed. | Decision ID, approved resources and conditions. |
| 4 | Data owner | At each configured measurement interval | Capture source population and results, validate completeness, and identify missing/late data. Zero denominator is not 100%; report not measurable with explanation. | Period result, source extract/reference and validation. |
| 5 | Objective owner | At each review and material failure | Compare results with target and baseline; investigate variance, escalate dependencies and propose action. Preserve original targets when approved changes are made; distinguish improvement from changed measurement. | Review decision, action links and target revision trail. |

## 4. Acceptance, holds and escalation

Another person can reproduce the result and explain the objective’s contribution to its linked risk. Target achievement does not by itself prove legal compliance or long-term effectiveness.

Hold performance claims where population, baseline or data integrity is unknown. Escalate missed milestones and harmful incentives. Do not lower a target retrospectively to turn a failure into a pass.

Measure overdue decisions/actions, missing mandatory evidence and failed control
executions in this process; define population and review interval locally. Do not
interpret “no reports” as “no problems.” Review both performance and reporting access.

## 5. Outputs, interfaces and records

Send scope/context decisions to risk owners; risk decisions to objective/control
owners; changed methods/forms to document control; performance and unresolved
issues to management review. The receiving owner acknowledges the handoff.
Record the incoming ID, outgoing ID, sender, receiver and acceptance or rejection.
Use one authoritative operational index for completed worksheets and evidence;
retain original event identity and template revision. The public examples are not
that operational index. The worksheet defines fields and filing rules.

## 6. Configure and test before use

Replace organizational placeholders; confirm scope, actual roles, lawful obligations,
approval limits, response times, retention/access and dependencies. Have relevant
specialists verify technical criteria. Execute one normal case and one held or
failed case with intended users; record findings before approval. Use
[the shared acceptance protocol](ORR-ASP-IMP-001_BEGINNER-KIT-ACCEPTANCE.md).

## Sources, tailoring and history

Original ORR learning design, based on the user-requested ORCA chain and practical
implementation needs. A purchased commercial pack was reviewed privately for
coverage and usability lessons before drafting; this is not a clean-room claim.
No vendor procedure, diagram, spreadsheet, clause text or completed record is
included. Source provenance and limits are recorded in ORR-REG-REL-002. Existing
ORCA attribution remains in the repository SOURCES.md. These are proposed internal
methods, not verified interpretations of ISO requirements or a certification checklist.

Adopters may change layout, terminology, software and proportional detail. Keep
traceable identity, accountable decisions, applicable obligations, evidence,
failure routes and approval boundaries. Unknown is not not-applicable. A mandatory
departure requires a recorded decision within legitimate authority; internal
acceptance cannot waive external duties. Use the linked document-control procedure.
